label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
**Dear Larkspur Lofts residents,**

I'm Jess Okafor in 5A. I'm writing to each of you directly because a note was posted in the lobby about me, and I would rather explain what happened in my own words than let a piece of paper in the stairwell speak for me.

On Saturday, October 31, at about 4:00 p.m., I took a short test flight with a new camera drone (a Halvard Mini 4) from the roof deck. The flight lasted roughly eleven minutes in total. I was testing the drone ahead of a wedding shoot in Dundee the following week, and the camera was pointed west the entire time, toward the Willamette River and the Fremont Bridge. It was never aimed at the building, at any windows, or into the courtyard, and no images of residents or interiors were captured.

I understand why it looked the way it did. A small buzzing aircraft hanging over a courtyard is genuinely unsettling if you don't know what it is or why it's there. A neighbor told me her grandchildren were frightened seeing it hover, and I'm sorry for that. It wasn't the intent, and I regret that I didn't think first about how the sight and the sound would land in a shared space.

There's one more thing I want to say plainly. The lobby note called me a "creep" and included my unit number. I don't know who wrote it, and I'm not going to speculate. But being labeled that way and identified in a common area where the whole building sees it felt wounding, and being discussed rather than spoken to isn't how I want to live here. If there was a concern about the drone, I would far rather hear it directly from a neighbor.

So, concretely, what I'm offering and what I'm promising:

- I will show the full, unedited flight footage to any resident who would like to see it. Knock on 5A any evening this week, or email me at jess.okafor@mailbox.example and I'll send the file or arrange a time to watch it together.
- I will not fly from the roof deck again until the board has had the chance to decide on a policy. In the meantime, I won't fly over the courtyard or in the direction of residents' windows.
- I would like drone use added to the agenda for the November 19 board meeting at 7:00 p.m. in the community room. Our current rules don't address drones, and I'd rather settle this as a group than in a lobby.

If something I did worried you, please come talk to me — knock on 5A, email me, or raise it at the meeting. I'd much rather resolve this as neighbors than as a note under a door.

Thank you for reading this, and for your patience.

Sincerely,
Jess Okafor
Unit 5A, Larkspur Lofts
